questions.q: What do great writers do despite doubts about their work, according to the summary?
a: They keep writing without worrying whether it is good
They wait until they feel confident to begin
They revise only when inspiration strikes
They study grammar before writing a draft
questions.why: The summary says believing you are meant to write leads to the practice that improves you.

questions.q: When does writing really begin to take off, according to the summary?
a: When you love the process more than the outcome
When you land your first publishing contract
When you finish a complete first draft
When other writers praise your work
questions.why: The summary stresses patience and attachment to the craft rather than results.

questions.q: Why does the summary recommend a fixed time and place for writing?
a: Repetition ties that time and place to creativity in the brain
It prevents friends from interrupting your work
It makes you write more words per session
It removes the need for a daily routine
questions.why: Consistent habits let inspiration arrive on schedule rather than by chance.

questions.q: What single quality did Lamott notice in the best writers she knew?
a: Commitment
Natural talent
Imagination
Confidence
questions.why: The summary says there was no secret code, only commitment to the work.

questions.q: What danger does the summary warn about when joining a writing group?
a: Harsh reviews can crush your confidence
Members may steal your best ideas
Groups often charge expensive fees
Groups discourage a daily writing habit
questions.why: It advises finding people who give useful tips without being merciless.
